verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The first crewed deep-space flight in over 50 years'; R2: 'For the first time since 1972, NASA is sending humans back on a path toward the Moon'; R3: 'Humans have not been to the moon since 1972'; R5: 'For the first time in more than 50 years, the United States is sending astronauts back toward the moon.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state or strongly imply Artemis II is the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years since Apollo (1972).

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the Orion spacecraft's life-support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA will test life-support systems and critical operations in deep space'; R4: 'life-support system checkouts'; R7: 'life-support and environmental control systems'; R8: 'test critical systems'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm testing of Orion's life-support systems during the mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II Launch Day Updates from NASA (.gov) highlights that the Artemis II mission sends astronauts around the Moon for the first time since 1972.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately 10-day mission around the Moon ... The first crewed deep-space flight in over 50 years'.
verifications.reasoning: R1 (the specified source) highlights first crewed mission around the Moon in over 50 years, equivalent to since 1972, but does not explicitly state 'since 1972'.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed test of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the first crewed flight of the SLS rocket'; R4: 'the most powerful rocket ridden by humans'; R7: 'NASA’s most powerful rocket ever built'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Artemis II as first crewed SLS launch, following uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed test of the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft'; R7: 'While Artemis I tested the spacecraft without astronauts, Artemis II will carry a crew'; R9: 'Artemis II was a test flight ... featuring the Orion spacecraft'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state first crewed Orion flight after uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis II checks life-support systems in deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test life-support systems ... in deep space'; R7: 'validate the life-support and environmental control systems ... in deep space'.
verifications.reasoning: Direct mentions of checking life-support in deep space.

verifications.claim: Artemis II checks navigation systems in deep space.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'manual piloting demos, trajectory correction maneuvers'; R7: 'navigation and communication capabilities'; R11: 'manual piloting and proximity operations'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention navigation, piloting, and trajectory tests in deep space context, but not explicitly 'checks navigation systems in deep space'.

verifications.claim: Artemis II checks thermal protection systems in deep space.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources discuss heat shield/thermal protection on reentry, not checks 'in deep space'; no mention of deep space testing of thermal systems.

verifications.claim: UVA Today "5 reasons why the Artemis II mission is a big deal" article notes that the Artemis II mission evaluates how deep space radiation impacts human health.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R3: 'more prone to cancer-causing radiation on the journey to the moon ... All Artemis missions going forward will be gathering data to make it safer ... Christina Koch, a mission specialist on Artemis II'.
verifications.reasoning: R3 (specified article) discusses radiation impacts and data gathering for Artemis missions including II via Koch, but not explicitly 'Artemis II evaluates how deep space radiation impacts human health'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will travel farther from Earth than any previous human mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'send the crew farther from Earth than any previous human mission'; R4: 'farther than anyone has ever traveled from our cosmic oasis'; R7: 'farther from Earth than any humans have traveled before'.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple direct statements confirm record distance.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests navigation to the lunar far side.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the only humans to have ever seen the far side of the moon'; R4: 'loop thousands of miles past the back side of the Moon'; R9: 'geological observations ... of the Moon's far side'.
verifications.reasoning: Mission involves far side flyby with navigation, but no explicit 'tests navigation to the lunar far side'; broader navigation tests mentioned.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'; R2: '10-day mission'; R3: '10-day journey'; consistently '10 days' or 'nearly 10-day' across sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to conclude with a Pacific Ocean splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California'; R7: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R8: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R9: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm Pacific Ocean splashdown conclusion.
